# Landing page proposal: night-shift bicycle repair shop

**Subject, audience, job:** the visitor has a broken bike after every other shop has closed. The page has to tell them within seconds that you are open and will fix it while they wait, then get them to the door.

## Design plan

**Colour**

| Name | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Late indigo | `#232A5C` | Page ground: a night sky, clearly blue rather than black |
| Tube white | `#EEF3E6` | Text on indigo: the slightly green white of a fluorescent tube |
| Sodium amber | `#F2A33A` | The primary action and the open/closed status only |
| Inner tube | `#14162B` | Text on amber and on light surfaces |
| Chalk blue | `#8E9AD6` | Secondary text, hairlines |

**Layout:** left-aligned throughout. The one photo is used once, large, as a lit window in a dark street; nothing else on the page competes with it.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [Shop name]                  Open now, to 12 │
│                                              │
│ Open until        ┌────────────────────────┐ │
│ midnight.         │                        │ │
│ Fixed while       │     workshop photo     │ │
│ you wait.         │     (the lit window)   │ │
│                   │                        │ │
│ [ Get directions ]└────────────────────────┘ │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Hours            │ Where to find us          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Mobile: photo, headline, then a "Get directions" bar fixed to the bottom.
```

**Principles**

- The page says only what is true: two facts, one photo.
- Amber means "act" or "open" and nothing else.
- There is one moment of motion and no other decoration.

**What I revised:** my first pass was near-black with a lamp-yellow accent and a giant "12:00" as the hero. That is the stock look for anything with "night" in the brief, so I moved the ground to indigo, split the light into two temperatures (tube white and sodium amber), and gave the hero to the photo and a plain sentence.

## Hero

- **Headline:** "Open until midnight. Fixed while you wait." It is both facts in two sentences, set large in one weight and colour, with no highlighted word.
- **Photo:** the workshop photo sits to the right with square corners, bleeding off the right edge so it reads as a window rather than a card. On load it flickers on like a fluorescent tube (two short stutters, then steady, under a second). With reduced motion set, it simply appears.
- **Status line:** the top right shows "Open now, closes at midnight" in amber, worked out from the visitor's clock. When the shop is closed it switches to chalk blue and gives the next opening time.

## Type direction

Use one family, Bricolage Grotesque. It is a variable grotesque with width and optical-size axes and slightly hand-cut shapes, which suits a workshop.

- **Headline:** condensed width, weight 700, 72px on desktop and 40px on mobile, line-height 1.0, tight tracking.
- **Body:** normal width, weight 400, 18px with 1.5 line-height, lines capped at about 60 characters.
- **Scale:** 18, 24, 36, 72.
- **Hours:** tabular figures so the times line up.
- **Case:** sentence case everywhere, with no all-caps labels and no monospace.

## Primary action

The button reads **"Get directions"** and opens the visitor's maps app with the shop as the destination. It is amber with inner-tube text and is the only filled button on the page. There is no booking form, because repairs happen while people wait and a form would imply otherwise.

## What I need from you

- The shop name and street address (the button depends on the address).
- Opening time and days. I only know the midnight close, so the status line cannot work without them.
- A look at the photo. If it was shot in daylight, the lit-window idea weakens and I would adjust the crop or the treatment.
- A phone number, if you want a secondary "Call the shop" link.

# Landing page proposal: night-shift bicycle repair shop

**Audience and job:** someone with a broken bike late in the evening. The page has to tell them in two seconds that the shop is open and they can ride home tonight, then get them to the door.

## Design plan

**Concept:** the shop is the one lit window on a dark street. The page is the street at dusk and the workshop photo is the only warm light source.

**Colour**

| Name | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Dusk blue | `#1F2A44` | Page background |
| Deep dusk | `#141C30` | Footer, photo surround |
| Lamp white | `#F3EEDF` | Headline and body text |
| Reflector amber | `#FFB000` | Primary action only |
| Chain steel | `#8E9AAF` | Secondary text, rules |

**Type:** one family, Archivo, in two widths.
- **Headline:** Archivo Expanded, weight 800, tight tracking, sentence case. It should read like a down-tube decal. About 72px on desktop and 40px on mobile, with a line-height of 1.0.
- **Body:** Archivo at normal width, weight 400, 18px with a 1.5 line-height and a maximum of 60 characters per line.
- **Scale:** 14 / 18 / 24 / 40 / 72.
- **Avoid:** all-caps labels, monospace details, and a single accented word in the headline.

**Layout:** left-aligned, asymmetric. The photo bleeds off the right and top edges, and the headline sits on the dusk blue and overlaps the photo's left edge.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Shop name                 ┌──────────────────┤
│                           │                  │
│ Open until midn│ight.     │  workshop photo  │
│ Fixed while you│wait.     │  (uncropped      │
│                           │   warm light)    │
│ ● Open now. Closes at     │                  │
│   midnight.               │                  │
│ [ Get directions ]        └──────────────────┤
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

On mobile, the photo goes on top at full width, with the headline, status and button stacked below. The button stays pinned to the bottom of the screen.

## Hero

- **Headline:** "Open until midnight. Fixed while you wait." These are the two real facts, set as two lines of equal weight.
- **Photo:** the single workshop photo, large and ungraded, with no dark overlay or gradient wash. Suggested alt text: "Inside the workshop at night."
- **Live status line:** this reads the visitor's clock and shows "Open now. Closes at midnight." with a small amber dot. Outside opening hours it switches to "Closed. Opens again at [time]."
- **Motion:** none, apart from the status dot fading in once on load. Reduced-motion settings are respected.

## Primary action

**"Get directions"** is a reflector-amber button with dark text, and it is the only amber element on the page. Repairs happen while customers wait, so the action is to turn up, not to book. It opens the visitor's maps app at the shop's address.

Below the hero, the page stays short: one paragraph on how waiting works, then the address and hours repeated with the same button.

## What I changed on review

My first instinct was a near-black page with a neon accent, which is the stock "night" look for any late-hours business. I changed it to dusk blue with the photo's own tungsten warmth as the light, and kept amber for the button only. Amber comes from bike reflectors, so it belongs to the subject.

## What I need from you

- The street address, for the directions button.
- The opening time, for the closed state.
- The shop name.
- The photo's orientation. The layout assumes landscape or square; a portrait photo would flip to a tall right-hand column.

- Which days the midnight closing applies to. I have not assumed "every night".

## Hero
- **Image:** the workshop photo runs full-bleed and fills the viewport. Darken the edges so the lit part of the photo glows, and keep it otherwise untreated, since it is the only image.

- **Subline:** "Repairs done while you wait."

- **Body and details:** a plain, sturdy sans such as Inter or IBM Plex Sans, at a generous size.
- **Hours:** set "Midnight" and any times in a monospace such as IBM Plex Mono, like a work ticket or timestamp.
- **Colour:** off-white text on near-black, plus one warm accent sampled from the lamp light in the photo. Use the accent only on the primary action.

## Primary action
**"Ride over now"** is a single accent-coloured button that opens directions to the shop. Visitors are likely to be on a phone with a broken bike late at night, and a while-you-wait shop makes its sale when they arrive, not when they fill in a form.

- On mobile, the button stays pinned to the bottom of the screen.
- It needs the shop's address, which is not in the facts supplied.
- A tap-to-call link would be a sensible secondary action if you have a phone number.

## Below the hero
Keep it to one short band that restates the two facts as a pair ("Until midnight / While you wait"), then a footer with the address. I would not add testimonials, price lists or service menus until there are real ones to show.
